Zina opened an account to save for a new car. Six months after opening the account, she made her first deposit of $\$1200$ and continued depositing $\$1200$ at the end of each six-month period.

Interest was paid at 3% per annum, compounded half-yearly.

How much was in Zina's account two years after first opening it? Give your answer to the nearest cent.

answer.short:
$\$4909.08$

Use four half-yearly periods: $V_0=0$ and $V_n=1.015V_{n-1}+1200$; iterate four times before rounding.
answer.worked:
There are $2\times2=4$ half-yearly periods, with interest rate $r=0.03\div2=0.015$ per period. Each deposit is made at the end of its period.

Let $V_n$ be the balance after $n$ deposits. Then $V_0=0$ and $V_n=1.015V_{n-1}+1200$.

$$\begin{align*}V_1&=1.015\times0+1200=1200\\V_2&=1.015\times1200+1200=2418\\V_3&=1.015\times2418+1200=3654.27\\V_4&=1.015\times3654.27+1200=4909.08405\end{align*}$$

After two years, Zina has $\$4909.08$, to the nearest cent.

children.prompt: $\$25\,000$ over 5 years at 6% p.a. compounded monthly, with monthly repayments.

answer.worked:
The monthly interest rate is $6\%\div12=0.5\%$. There are $5\times12=60$ repayments. Let $M$ be the monthly repayment.

Start: $25\,000$.

After the first repayment: $25\,000(1.005)-M$.

After the second repayment:
$$\begin{align*}V_2&=[25\,000(1.005)-M](1.005)-M\\V_2&=25\,000(1.005)^2-M(1.005)-M.\end{align*}$$
After the 60th repayment:
$$V_{60}=25\,000(1.005)^{60}-M(1.005)^{59}-\cdots-M.$$
The subtracted terms form a geometric series with first term $M$, ratio $1.005$ and 60 terms. When the loan is repaid, $V_{60}=0$.
$$\begin{align*}0&=25\,000(1.005)^{60}-M\frac{(1.005)^{60}-1}{1.005-1}\\M\frac{(1.005)^{60}-1}{0.005}&=25\,000(1.005)^{60}\\M&=\frac{25\,000(1.005)^{60}(0.005)}{(1.005)^{60}-1}\\M&\approx\$483.32.\end{align*}$$
Total paid: $\$483.32\times60=\$28\,999.20$.

Interest paid: $\$28\,999.20-\$25\,000=\$3999.20$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: $\$12\,000$ over 4 years at 8% p.a. compounded quarterly, with quarterly repayments.

answer.worked:

Start: $12\,000$.

After the second repayment:
$$\begin{align*}V_2&=[12\,000(1.02)-M](1.02)-M\\V_2&=12\,000(1.02)^2-M(1.02)-M.\end{align*}$$
After the 16th repayment:
$$V_{16}=12\,000(1.02)^{16}-M(1.02)^{15}-\cdots-M.$$
The subtracted terms form a geometric series with first term $M$, ratio $1.02$ and 16 terms. When the loan is repaid, $V_{16}=0$.
$$\begin{align*}0&=12\,000(1.02)^{16}-M\frac{(1.02)^{16}-1}{1.02-1}\\M\frac{(1.02)^{16}-1}{0.02}&=12\,000(1.02)^{16}\\M&=\frac{12\,000(1.02)^{16}(0.02)}{(1.02)^{16}-1}\\M&\approx\$883.80.\end{align*}$$

children.label: a

answer.worked:
There are $2040-2021+1=20$ contributions.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Total invested}&=20(10\,000)\\\text{Total invested}&=\$200\,000.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate, correct to the nearest dollar, the amount to which the 2021 payment has grown by the beginning of 2041.

answer.worked:
The first payment grows for $2041-2021=20$ years.

$$\begin{align*}V&=10\,000(1.1)^{20}\\V&\approx\$67\,275\quad\text{(nearest dollar).}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the total value of the fund when it is paid out on 1 January 2041, correct to the nearest dollar.

answer.worked:
On 1 January 2041, the contributions have grown to

$$10\,000(1.1)^{20}+10\,000(1.1)^{19}+\cdots+10\,000(1.1).$$

In increasing order of powers, this geometric series has $a=10\,000(1.1)$, $r=1.1$ and $n=20$.

$$\begin{align*}FV&=\frac{10\,000(1.1)(1.1^{20}-1)}{1.1-1}\\FV&\approx\$630\,025\quad\text{(nearest dollar).}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: The person wants to reach a total value of $\$1\,000\,000$ in superannuation. For this part, suppose the annual contributions of $\$10\,000$ continue at the beginning of each year beyond 2040. Measure the value at the end of each investment year, before the next contribution.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Find a formula for $A_n$, the value of the investment after $n$ years.

answer.worked:
After $n$ years,

$$A_n=10\,000(1.1)^n+10\,000(1.1)^{n-1}+\cdots+10\,000(1.1).$$

In increasing order of powers, this is a geometric series with first term $10\,000(1.1)$, common ratio $1.1$ and $n$ terms.

$$\begin{align*}A_n&=\frac{10\,000(1.1)(1.1^n-1)}{1.1-1}\\A_n&=\frac{10\,000(1.1)(1.1^n-1)}{0.1}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Show that the target is exceeded when $1.1^n>\dfrac{10}{1.1}+1$.

children.label: iii
children.prompt: At the end of which investment year will the superannuation first exceed $\$1\,000\,000$? Give the calendar year as well.

answer.short: The 25th investment year: the end of 2045.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}n&>\frac{\log\left(\frac{10}{1.1}+1\right)}{\log1.1}\\n&>24.253809\ldots\end{align*}$$

The least whole number is $n=25$. The first investment year is 2021, so the 25th is $2021+25-1=2045$. The target is first exceeded at the end of 2045, immediately before 1 January 2046.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Suppose instead that the person wanted to achieve the same total investment of $\$1\,000\,000$ after only 20 years. What annual contribution, paid at the beginning of each year, would produce this amount? Give your answer to the nearest cent. (Hint: Let $M$ be the amount of each contribution.)

Let the annual contribution be $M$. After 20 years, the value is

children.prompt: Find the amount of each monthly repayment to the nearest cent.

Loan amount:
$$\begin{aligned}P&=10000-1500\\P&=8500\end{aligned}$$
Monthly growth factor:
$$r=1+\frac{0.18}{12}=1.015$$
Number of repayments:
$$n=4\times12=48$$
Let $M$ be the monthly repayment.

Start: $8500$.

After the first repayment: $8500r-M$.

After the second repayment:
$$\begin{aligned}(8500r-M)r-M&=8500r^2-Mr-M\end{aligned}$$

content.prompt: A couple take out a $\$250\,000$ mortgage on a house, and they agree to pay the bank $\$2000$ per month. The interest rate on the loan is 7.2% per annum, compounded monthly, and the contract requires that the loan be paid off within 20 years.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Let $A_n$ be the balance on the loan after $n$ months. Find a series expression for $A_n$.

answer.worked:
Monthly growth factor:
$$r=1+\frac{0.072}{12}=1.006.$$
Start: $250000$.

1st repayment: $250000r-2000$.

2nd repayment: $250000r^2-2000r-2000$.

After $n$ repayments:
$$A_n=250000r^n-2000r^{n-1}-2000r^{n-2}-\cdots-2000.$$
The repayments form a geometric series with first term $2000$, common ratio $r=1.006$ when read in reverse order, and $n$ terms.

Using the geometric-series sum:
$$\begin{align*}A_n&=250000r^n-\frac{2000(r^n-1)}{r-1}\\A_n&=250000(1.006)^n-\frac{2000(1.006^n-1)}{0.006}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the amount owing on the loan at the end of the tenth year, to the nearest dollar, and state whether this is more or less than half the amount borrowed.

answer.short: $\$162\,498$; more than half the amount borrowed.
answer.worked:
At the end of 10 years, $n=120$.
$$\begin{align*}A_{120}&=250000(1.006)^{120}-\frac{2000(1.006^{120}-1)}{0.006}\\A_{120}&=162498.495266\ldots\\A_{120}&\approx\$162\,498.\end{align*}$$
Half the amount borrowed is $\$125\,000$, so this is more than half.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find $A_{240}$ to the nearest dollar, and hence show that the loan is actually paid out in less than twenty years.

answer.short: $A_{240}\approx-\$16\,881$; the loan is paid out in less than 20 years.
answer.worked:
At the end of 20 years, $n=240$.
$$\begin{align*}A_{240}&=250000(1.006)^{240}-\frac{2000(1.006^{240}-1)}{0.006}\\A_{240}&=-16881.169433\ldots\\A_{240}&\approx-\$16\,881.\end{align*}$$
The negative modelled balance means that continuing the scheduled repayments for 240 months would overpay the loan. Therefore it is paid out in less than 20 years.

children.label: e
children.prompt: If it is paid out after $n$ months, show that $1.006^n=4$, and hence that $n=\dfrac{\log4}{\log1.006}$.

children.label: f
children.prompt: Find how many months early the loan is paid off.

answer.worked:
$$n=\frac{\log4}{\log1.006}=231.741516\ldots$$
The loan is paid off at the 232nd monthly repayment, with a smaller final payment.
$$240-232=8.$$
Therefore it is paid off 8 months early.

entries.description: Types of Annuity Problems

Ordinary annuity
End-of-period contributions with end-of-period compounding.
\(FV=a\left[\frac{(1+r)^n-1}{(1+r)-1}\right]\)

Annuity due
Start-of-period contributions with end-of-period compounding.
Set up geometric series and multiply by one more of \((1+r)\):
\(FV=a\left[\frac{(1+r)^n-1}{(1+r)-1}\right](1+r)\)

Annuity with starting lump sum
Split account into two parts, the original lump sum, \(PV\), which earns compound interest separately, and the ordinary annuity of the regular contributions.
\(FV=PV(1+r)^n+a\left[\frac{(1+r)^n-1}{(1+r)-1}\right]\)

Annuity withdrawal problem:
Treat your starting amount as if you never touch it and continue to compound.
Treat your withdrawals as a parallel timeline and subtract: every time you take money out, you lose out on the future interest that specific cash would have earned.
\(FV=PV(1+r)^n-a\left[\frac{(1+r)^n-1}{(1+r)-1}\right]\)
